title: The most extreme places
text: Our planet has some places where it is very difficult to live. Right now, scientists are working in many of them. They are trying to understand how life survives in extreme conditions.

Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth. In 1983 a station there recorded minus eighty-nine degrees. Today, researchers are living in bases on the ice. In winter the sun does not come up for months, so they are living in the dark.

Death Valley, in the United States, is one of the hottest places. In 1913 the temperature reached fifty-seven degrees. At the moment, tourists are visiting it in cars with air conditioning, and they are drinking a lot of water.
The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest place. Some parts have not seen rain for hundreds of years. The air is so clear that astronomers are using giant telescopes there to look at the stars.

Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world: almost nine thousand meters. Up there, there is very little oxygen. Every spring, climbers are trying to reach the top, but it is a very dangerous adventure.

grammar.title: Grammar: the present continuous
grammar.rule: Use the present continuous (am / is / are + -ing) for actions happening now or around now.
items: Right now, a researcher ___ living on the ice.
Tourists are ___ a lot of water.
The climbers ___ trying to reach the top.
